Order 
Per: Justice Vivek Agarwal Heard on I.A.No.2967/2025, which is first application under Section 389(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (for short "Cr.P.C") for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the appellant Neeraj Jharia.
2. Learned counsel for the appellant prays for withdrawal of the aforesaid application.
3. I.A.No.2967/2025 is dismissed as withdrawn.
4. With the consent of learned counsel for the parties, this appeal is finally heard.

5. This appeal under Section 374(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (for short "Cr.P.C") is filed being aggrieved of judgment dated 4.7.2024 passed by learned II Additional Sessions Judge-Lakhnadon, District Seoni in Special Case No.109/2021 convicting the appellant Neeraj Jharia for NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:50732 2 CRA-436-2025 the offence under Sections 363, 366 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (for short "I.P.C") and Sections 5(l)/6 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (for short "POCSO Act") and sentencing him to undergo rigorous imprisonment for two years, three years and twenty years with fine of Neeraj Jharia vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53174911/
1 Rs.2,000/-, Rs.3,000/-, Rs.10,000/- and in default of payment of fine to undergo additional rigorous imprisonment for two months, two months and three months respectively with a further direction to run all the jail sentences concurrently.

sentences.text: The prosecution case in short is that on 19.8.2021, the father of the victim had lodged a report at Police Station Chhapara that some unknown person abducted his daughter on which Crime No.383/2021 for the offence under Section 363 of the I.P.C was registered.
During investigation, on 28.8.2021, the victim was recovered.
Her statement under Section 164 of the Cr.P.C was recorded.
She was subjected to medical examination.
Her birth certificate etc was seized.
The offence under Sections 366, 376, 376(2)(n) of the I.P.C and Sections 3, 4, 5(l), 6 of the POCSO Act was thereafter added.
The charge sheet was filed.
The appellant abjured his guilt and pleaded complete innocence.
The prosecution examined as many as twelve witnesses and proved thirty one exhibits on record but the accused did not examine any witness in support of his defence.
7. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the appellant is innocent.
He has been falsely implicated in this case.
The victim is a consenting adult.

From the testimony of the victim given by her under Section 164 of the Cr.P.C as contained in Exhibit P/3, it is evident that she was in love NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:50732 3 CRA-436-2025 relationship with the appellant and they wanted to marry each other but because of obstacle posed by her family members, she had left her home on 3.8.2021 at about 11:30 PM.
Reading from the testimony of PW.3, who is mother of the victim, it is submitted that the victim was an adult at the time of the incident.

8. Learned Government Advocate for the State supports the impugned judgment and submits that Exhibit P/10 is birth certificate of the victim so also Exhibit P/13 is her mark sheet of Class-IX whereas Exhibit P/18 is her Dakhil Kharij Register whereby her date of birth is mentioned as 4.4.2005, therefore, she was minor at the time of the incident.
9. We have heard learned counsel for the parties and gone through the record.
10. The birth certificate (Exhibit P/10) is with regard to a male child and not with regard to a female child, therefore, that document is of no consequence.

As far as marksheet of Class-IX (Exhibit P/13)
is concerned, the victim in her testimony admits that she was studying in Class-XI but the Investigating Officer has failed to seize her Class-X marksheet, which could have been a better proof of the date of birth of the victim.

11 . As far as Dakhil Kharij Register (Exhibit P/18) is concerned,
School Teacher Ayub Shah (PW.5) admits that the date of birth of the victim was recorded on the basis of a slip received from Aganwadi but further admits that the said slip from Aganwadi is not enclosed alongwith the Dakhil Kharij Register.

In Paragraph No.7, School Teacher Ayub Shah (PW.5) states that Dakhil Kharij Register should have been in a sequential order and that order NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:50732 4 CRA-436-2025 is disrupted, which causes a dent to the credibility of the Dakhil Kharij Register.

12. The mother of the victim (PW.3) in Paragraph No.9 of her cross- examination admits that her marriage was performed in the year 2002 and the victim was born immediately after one year of her Neeraj Jharia vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53174911/
2 marriage.

sentences.text: She also admits that age of her husband is 44-45 years and their marriage was performed 20- 22 years prior to the date of the incident.
Thus, it is evident that the victim was an adult at the time of the incident.

13. When all these facts are taken into consideration then the finding of conviction recorded by the learned Trial Court overlooking the testimony of the mother of the victim (PW.3) cannot be given a seal of approval.

Once the victim was an adult and it is evident from her statement recorded under Section 164 of the Cr.P.C that she was a willing and consenting party then consensual relationship between two adults cannot be said to be a crime either under Section 375 of the I.P.C or under Section 3/5 of the POCSO Act.
14. Accordingly, this appeal is allowed.

the impugned judgment of conviction of the appellant Neeraj Jharia passed by learned II Additional Sessions Judge-Lakhnadon, District Seoni on 4.7.2024 in Special Case No.109/2021 for the offence under Sections 363, 366 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and Section 5(l)/6 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 is hereby set aside.
